title: A hook refuses `git show <rev>:<path>` of a file over a size cap unless the output is bounded
why: An unbounded git show of a large file dumps hundreds of kilobytes into a session and wastes its reading (a 238 KB dump by backlog-drain).
source: Coordinator 15:36 CST Nov 13, from the backlog-drain mistake (its record names the incident). Rule tokens-never-load-whole-doc.
note: Filed 15:36 CST Nov 13. A guard: refuse `git show <rev>:<path>` of a file over a size cap unless the output is piped to something bounded (head, sed range). The cap is a cost line, measured, not a fixed number (owner R37). The guard that would have stopped the mistake is this step. A guard change: test-author red case first, builder, reviewer; the incident record is the lane's to cite. Past rulings not checked.
